messages:
alex: seeing a bunch of GPU nodes go NotReady / NoSchedule in eu-west1, autoscaler keeps bouncing but capacity not usable :grimacing:
neha: alert from infra-bot? can you paste `kubectl get nodes` output and the daemonset logs?
alex: infra-bot posted alert earlier, but here's quick `kubectl get nodes` snippet:
```
NAME                            STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-eu-1-nodepool-7d9f2        NotReady   <none>   12m   v1.29.3
gpu-eu-1-nodepool-9c2a1        NoSchedule <none>   11m   v1.29.3
```
sam: can you grab `kubectl describe node` for one of the NotReady ones? usually device-plugin registration errors are logged there
alex: from `kubectl describe node gpu-eu-1-nodepool-7d9f2`:
```
Taints:             node.kubernetes.io/not-ready:NoSchedule
Events:
  Type     Reason                   Age   From                     Message
  ----     ------                   ----  ----                     -------
  Warning  DevicePluginUnhealthy    10m   kubelet, gpu-eu-1        device plugin failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc: plugin init timeout
```
kai: that looks like the NVIDIA device-plugin failing to start/init. any recent AMI/kernel/driver changes pushed to that nodepool?
alex: we rolled a node image yesterday (kernel 6.x) and bumped the `nvidia-driver-package` in the startup script. Not sure if driver version and kernel module mismatch is the root cause
neha: autoscaler behavior: it's provisioning more nodes but they never register as schedulable because the device plugin doesn't register GPUs -> cluster thinks capacity exists but schedulable pods see no GPU resources. autoscaler then throttles due to failures -> backoff cycle :/
sam: grabbing daemonset logs now, here's the relevant lines from `kubectl logs -n kube-system nvidia-device-plugin-7d9f2`:
```
E0901 08:22:10.123 1 server.go:112] failed to init plugin: failed to create nvml handle: driver not loaded
E0901 08:22:10.124 1 server.go:118] device plugin initialization timed out
```
kai: "driver not loaded" usually means kernel module didn't build/attach. Could be dkms failure on boot or missing prebuilt module for that kernel. Also seen on preemptible images when boot script races.
alex: lots of these are preemptible/preempt pools, startup script runs `apt install nvidia-driver` which triggers module build. If autoscaler brings up 20 nodes at once, they all try to compile modules and some fail due to IO wait / package cache races
neha: that explains the autoscales spikes + transient billing. we should avoid autoscaler burst bringing up too many GPU nodes concurrently. options: limit `maxSurge`/parallelism, set `maxNodeProvisioningPerSecond` at provider, or pre-warm a small standing pool (1-2 nodes)
sam: immediate mitigation: mark nodepool with `scaleDownDisabled` or set cluster-autoscaler flag `--scale-down-delay-after-add=10m` to stop immediate churn. also add a liveness check to device-plugin so kubelet doesn't taint NotReady while plugin restarts?
kai: longer term: change startup to use prebuilt kernel modules from our artifact bucket matching the AMI/kernel combo, fall back to dkms only if no match. Also add a jitter to driver install step and a systemd unit that waits for `modprobe nvidia` to succeed before kubelet registers. Example systemd snippet:
```ini
[Unit]
After=network-online.target
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/install-nvidia.sh
ExecStartPost=/bin/systemctl restart kubelet
```
alex: will test that workflow on a staging pool. if we can reduce the parallel installs, we should stop the device-plugin init timeouts
neha: FYI finance pinged: cost this morning spiked 38% in eu-west1 because autoscaler kept provisioning then evicting. they asked for a postmortem and cost mitigation plan :money_with_wings:
sam: for the short window we can also add a taint `node.kubernetes.io/gpu-booting=true:NoSchedule` in the node startup script until the plugin is healthy, then remove it. prevents scheduler from trying to use nodes prematurely and triggering pod evictions/dups.
kai: also consider `--balance-similar-node-groups` off for CA or tune `--max-node-provision-time` so CA recognizes nodes stuck provisioning and stops blasting more nodes into same pool
alex: action items: 1) test systemd prebuilt-module flow on staging (assign: alex) 2) add startup taint pattern and remove on plugin ready (assign: sam) 3) throttle autoscaler bursts and pre-warm 1 spare node in eu-west1 (assign: neha) 4) finance writeup about cost spike (assign: kai)
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1883, severity P2 — tagging oncall and finance.
neha: thanks — looping in oncall for evening watch. I'll update the incident with timeline after staging run. :thumbsup:
